If the owner records a compatibility acceptance, require for every RAW32 release: a fresh PIN entry on-device (not session unlock), a per-session RAW32 cap (e.g. 3) in SRAM, a 'NO INTENT - dapp hash only' danger interstitial before the hash pages, and companion-visible counter in OFFCHAIN_STATUS so audits can see RAW32 use.
improvements.rationale: Trezor core ships NO blind typed-hash path at all (only legacy T1 has EthereumSignTypedHash); Ledger requires blind signing to be disabled by default. pq1 currently has no switch at all, so a production image necessarily carries the downgrade oracle the CLAUDE.md scope paragraph warns about. improvements.title: S-world spending-policy guard (Coldcard SSSP-class) evaluated before confirm
improvements.threat: Clear signing shows the truth but does not stop a coerced ($5 wrench), hurried, or socially-engineered user, nor a compromised companion that waits for a legitimate unlock; a single approved page can move everything.
improvements.proposal: Add an owner-configured policy record (page-123-style durable config, NOT per-signature state): per-op max native value and per-token max amount, recipient allowlist (addresses + 'self' = any account_index CREATE2 address recomputed in S-world), chain allowlist, minimum wall-clock/TIM interval between releases, and 'Safe mgmt / unlimited approve forbidden' toggles. Evaluate on the parsed S-stack copy BEFORE pick_sign_pages; out-of-policy → refuse without explanation (Coldcard semantics). Policy edits require a separate Policy PIN entered on-device whose compromise cannot export the seed, with an optional lockdown bit that makes the policy immutable until a wipe.
improvements.rationale: Coldcard ships exactly this and assumes the attacker already holds the main PIN; Ledger/Trezor have no on-device policy. The repo's own roadmap names 'on-device policy guard (refuse out-of-policy ops before confirm)' as a security differentiator but nothing is implemented. It is the only way to get module-grade limits on PQSmartWallet, where no on-chain module can ever be installed.

improvements.title: Render paymaster semantics: carry raw paymasterAndData, show sponsor identity and fee-token pull
improvements.threat: The device signs keccak/sha256(paymasterAndData) but never sees the bytes: it cannot show WHO sponsors gas or that an ERC-20 fee-token paymaster will debit USDC up to a max cost. A compromised companion can route through a hostile paymaster; the user sees only '! PAYMASTER SET / may debit tokens'.
improvements.proposal: Pre-launch wire change (input format only; on-chain output unchanged): replace the 32-byte `paymaster_and_data_hash` input with `[pm_len(2)][paymasterAndData ≤ 256 B]`, compute the hash in S-world, and render: paymaster address with NAMES_DB-verified name ('+' sentinel), mode decode for pinned providers (Pimlico ERC20PaymasterV06: fee token + exchange-rate/max-cost words → 'Gas paid in USDC, max 1.23'), 'Sponsored (no debit)' for verifying-paymaster shapes, and a loud '! UNKNOWN PAYMASTER' danger page otherwise. Cross-check: an inner `approve(spender==paymaster)` in the same UserOp renders the spender as 'PAYMASTER' with the amount, refusing unlimited unless the policy (CS-03) allows.

The roadmap already identifies this and the unlimited-approve(paymaster) hazard.

improvements.title: Generic EIP-712 field walker gated by a registry-known-domain omission filter (Bloom twin) and empty-domain refusal
improvements.threat: Any typed-data request for a dapp without a curated ERC-7730 EIP-712 descriptor is signable only as RAW32 (blind); users are pushed to the worst tier precisely for long-tail dapps, and a hostile companion can strip the descriptor from a registry-known domain only if there is a generic path — so the two must land together.
improvements.proposal: (1) Build a 16 KiB Bloom of every registry-declared (chain_id, verifyingContract, primaryType-hash) tuple (same dbgen pipeline and 25% occupancy cap as known_calls); a kind-2/3 request whose domain is Bloom-positive but carries no bound descriptor hard-refuses ('7730 eip712 proof needed'), exactly mirroring the contract-call filter. (2) For Bloom-negative domains, add a structural walker: render EVERY leaf (no 'show more' skipping), label by field name from the companion-supplied type string whose hash the device recomputes into the EIP-712 typeHash (so names are bound to the signed hash), refuse arrays-of-arrays, nested EIP712Domain members, missing chainId/verifyingContract, non-UTF-8 strings; banner '! NO INTENT / structure only'; final Eip712Final ERC-8213 page; chord/hold after last page. (3) Keep RAW32 (CS-01) off.
improvements.rationale: Trezor and Ledger both render arbitrary EIP-712 generically; pq1 refuses, which is sound but drives long-tail dapps to RAW32. The walker is NOT semantic clear-signing (no intent claim) but is strictly better than a 32-byte hash, and the Bloom twin preserves the 'registry-known shape either clear-signs or refuses' contract for typed data, which today holds only for contract calls.

improvements.title: On-chain intent commitment: PQSmartWallet verifies a canonical intent digest for native shapes
improvements.threat: Today WYSIWYS is a device property only: a faulted/compromised render path (FI on the dispatcher, a future renderer bug of the LSB-024 class) can produce a valid C10 signature over calldata whose semantics were never shown, and the chain accepts it.
improvements.proposal: Design spike then implement: extend `executeWithOffchainCount` (pre-launch; no address change constraints beyond re-pinning codehashes) with an `intentDigest` argument; the firmware sets it to sha256 over a frozen canonical encoding of the rendered intent class + operands it actually displayed (e.g. `ETH_TRANSFER‖chain‖to‖value`, `ERC20_TRANSFER‖token‖to‖amount`, `ERC20_APPROVE‖token‖spender‖amount`, `BLIND‖calldataDigest`); the contract recomputes the digest from (target,value,data) with a tiny on-chain decoder for the native shapes (ERC-20 selectors, empty data, else BLIND) and reverts on mismatch. Because the digest is in callData it is covered by the existing userOpHash/sphincsDigest — no verifier change. Companion fixtures + Kani harness 'rendered operands == committed operands'.
improvements.rationale: Unique lever: pq1 controls both the signer and the wallet contract, which Ledger/Trezor never do. It converts 'the device showed X' into 'the chain will only execute what the device committed to', closing the gap between transcript proofs (device) and execution (chain) for the shapes that carry >80% of drain value.

improvements.title: C10-signed catalogue refresh with monotonic data-version floor, decoupled from firmware images
improvements.threat: Descriptor/token/name roots are compiled in, so catalogue freshness = firmware update cadence; ERC-8176 attestations are brittle (any label change invalidates the hash) and the registry governance moved to the EF in 2026-05. The clear set C will drift stale fast, pushing users to blind tiers, and invariant #10's 'never trust a firmware update again' makes frequent images undesirable.
improvements.proposal: Define a `PQCAT` bundle: {data_version u32, ERC7730_DESCRIPTORS_ROOT, ERC20_DB_ROOT, NAMES_DB_ROOT, SELECTOR_DB_ROOT, KNOWN_CALLS Bloom hash, P73S receipt} signed with SPHINCS+C10 by a vendor catalogue key whose pubkey is pinned in the secure image (single algorithm, invariant #5). New CMD_CATALOGUE_UPDATE (PIN-unlocked, on-device confirm showing data_version + 8-word fingerprint of the bundle) verifies the C10 signature in S-world, requires data_version > the floor stored in a dedicated config page, writes the roots to that page, and the dispatcher reads roots from the page (falling back to compiled-in only if the page is blank). Leaves keep a type-domain byte so a token leaf can never parse as a descriptor leaf. Rollback of data_version refused; firmware images carry a minimum floor.
improvements.rationale: Trezor's external-definitions model (Merkle + CoSi root + one-month freshness floor + built-ins override) decouples coverage from firmware; pq1 keeps stronger provenance (pinned roots) but zero agility. A C10-signed bundle keeps the one-primitive policy and avoids Trezor's regression to a single CoSi signer by using one PQ key with an on-device fingerprint ceremony.
